question.leadin: Answer some questions about very badly named military operations.
question.text: Operations Breakfast, Lunch, Snack, Dinner, Supper, and Dessert were launched to bomb this country neighboring Vietnam during the Vietnam War.
question.answerHtml: Kingdom of Cambodia [or le Royaume du Cambodge, or Prĕəh Riəciənaacak Kampuciə; accept Democratic Kampuchea or Kâmpŭchéa Prâcheathippadey; accept Srok Khmae]
question.clue: Another temple in this country has large towers adorned with faces called Bayon.

swap.leadin: This woman won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize but could not accept it in person, as the ruling military junta held her under house arrest.
swap.text: Name this activist and politician who became State Counsellor of her country in 2016. Since her rise to power, she has been heavily criticized for her inaction against the persecution of the Rohingya people.
swap.answerHtml: Aung San Suu Kyi ([ong sahn soo chee], but be lenient) (prompt on “Suu” or “Kyi” alone)
swap.clue: This leader allegedly called two Reuters journalists "traitors" after they were arrested while investigating the Inn Din Massacre.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Southeast Asian independence movements.
question.text: David Marshall campaigned for the independence of this country. Reforms by its first leader, Lee Kwan Yew, made this city-state one of the four "Asian Tigers" with rapidly-growing economies.
question.clue: HMS Prince of Wales led a naval group named Force Z assigned to protect this country that was destroyed by Japanese airstrikes prior to an invasion by Tomoyuki Yamashita's forces.

swap.text: The accusations of Duterte "death squads" come from when he was Mayor of Davao City on this Philippine island, the main home of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front.
swap.clue: Historically, the Sulu Sultanate controlled large portions of this island's Zamboanga Peninsula.

question.text: Many battles of the Pacific theater of World War II were fought in this country, including the Battle of Leyte Gulf and the Battle of Luzon.
question.clue: This country's Moro people led a lengthy guerilla war against its colonizers.

swap.leadin: This leader converted a high school into the s21 ("s-twenty-one") prison.
swap.text: Name this man, who called himself "Brother Number One" while leading the Khmer Rouge. ("Kuh-mair roozh")
swap.clue: Relations between this man's government and its Eastern neighbor deteriorated during his rule, leading to a Vietnamese invasion that ousted him from power.

question.leadin: The Thirtieth of September Movement was an attempted coup against this leader.
question.text: Name this leader who established a system of "Guided Democracy." This first president of Indonesia hosted the Bandung conference, which eventually led to the development of the Non-Aligned Movement.
question.clue: His state philosophy was known as Pancasila, or Five Principles, and he was forced to declare his nationa's independence by a 1945 kidnapping.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain conflict.
swap.text: The First Indochina War saw a major French defeat at this battle, in which French paratroopers set up 7 forts named after the commanding officer's former mistresses, and were besieged by a superior Vietnamese artillery.
swap.clue: It began with a surprise attack that took the northeast headquarter Beatrice, after which the headquarters Gabrielle and Anne-Marie fell, marking the defeat of Christian de Castries.

question.leadin: Southward expansion during this dynasty occurred through the don dien system, by which hybrid agricultural-military colonies facilitated rice farming.
question.text: Name this longest-lasting Vietnamese ruling dynasty which reached its height under Thanh Tong, who completed the conquest of the Champa Kingdom.
question.answerHtml: Later Le Dynasty [do NOT accept "Earlier Le Dynasty"]
question.clue: During this dynasty's rule, Alexander de Rhodes popularized a Latin script that would eventually replace Chu Nom.

swap.leadin: The first rulers of this modern-day country were the legendary Hung kings.
swap.text: Name this country, also home to kingdoms like Champa and Funan. Many of its major civilizations were established on the Mekong River.
swap.clue: Gia Long was the first emperor of its last ruling dynasty, and during the early 20th century, this country adopted the Quoc Ngu writing system.

question.text: The protest on Kent State was specifically directed against this decision announced by Richard Nixon on April 30, which controversially expanded the Vietnam War to another country.
question.answerHtml: invasion of the Kingdom of Cambodia [or Cambodian campaign]
question.answer: invasion of the Kingdom of Cambodia
question.clue: The protestors killed in the Kent State shootings of 1970 were protesting this specific facet of the Vietnam War, which had been made public by President Nixon on April 30.

swap.leadin: The death of a monarch with this name was initially ruled an accident despite shots to his back.
swap.text: Give this regnal name of Ananda Mahidol, whose predecessor was criticized during a 1932 constitutional revolution. All rulers of the Rattanakosin ("rat-tan-uh-KOH-sin") kingdom took on this regnal name.
swap.clue: The first king of this name ascended to the position after executing his predecessor, King Taksin, while the fourth ruler of this name died of malaria after watching a solar eclipse he had predicted.

question.leadin: Answer the following related to the Taungoo ("TOWN-goo") Empire, an early modern state in Southeast Asia.
question.text: The Taungoo Empire and its successor states, including the Konbaung dynasty, were both based out of this modern-day country later governed from Mandalay by the British.
question.clue: Many of a religious minority from this country have been forced to move to Bhasan Char silt island in a neighbouring country.

swap.text: Excessive taxation imposed under the Toungoo ("TOWN-goo") dynasty in this modern-day country transformed its Irrawaddy delta region into what one historian termed a "depopulated desert."
swap.answerHtml: Myanmar [or Republic of the Union of Myanmar; accept Burma]
swap.clue: A 16th century temple in this country noted for its sandstone blocks fitted together without mortar was built to commemorate a king's naval victory over Portugal.

question.leadin: Erica Fox Brindley discussed the "sparse" references to the Yue ("yweh") in a source about this event, which gives little information about its central participants besides calling one "heroic and courageous"
question.text: Name this 40s CE event suppressed by the general Ma Yuan ("mah ywen"). Some native chronicles claim that its leaders committed suicide in the Hat Giang ("haat zaang") to avoid surrender.
question.answerHtml: Trưng sisters’ rebellion [accept clear equivalents; accept answers with Zheng or Cheng in place of “Trưng”]
question.clue: Following this conflict's 43 A.D. conclusion, two copper columns were erected to mark the southern boundary of the territory of the Guangwu Emperor.

swap.leadin: The Ja Thak Wa uprising in 1835 occurred in protest to Emperor Minh Mang's annexation of this ethnicity's last autonomous state.
swap.text: Name this Austronesian ethnic group. They were the main ethnic group in central Vietnam and led a state of the same name until 1471, when its capital of Vijaya was captured by Đai Viet.
swap.clue: Upon conquering the neighbouring Funan Kingdom, Shaivism became the state religion, and the kingdom was involved in the Spice Route as a producer of aloe.

question.text: The second, or "restored" dynasty of this name, was the frst to re-unify Burma afer the fall of the Pagan kingdom and had its capital at Ava around 1606. The frst dynasty by this name arose in Burma under Mingyinyo near the end of the Ava kingdom and conquered the Mohnyin Shan peoples.

swap.leadin: The present-day capital of this region, Sittwe ("sit-tway"), has a name meaning "place where war meets," as it was the site of a battle during the conquest of this region's Mrauk U ("muh-RAO oo") kingdom.
swap.text: Name this coastal region. After gaining control of this region in the Treaty of Yandabo, the British encouraged Bengali laborers to settle it throughout the 19th century.
swap.clue: This region once ruled by the Kingdom of Mrauk U [myow oo]. The Mughal Empire recaptured the city of Chittagong from an alliance of the Portuguese and pirates from this region.

question.leadin: In 1857 Chinese laborers revolted against one of these rulers after he instituted a high opium tax, and this dynasty had its capital at Kuching.
question.text: Name this dynasty that controlled the Miri oilfields and ruled Serawak from the mid-1800s to the mid-1900s.
question.clue: The Japanese invasion of Borneo ended the rule of this dynasty, which began when the Sultan of Brunei rewarded the patriarch of this family with the Raj of Sarawak after crushing a tribal rebellion.

swap.text: An eponymous general overthrew Taksin the Great and took the name Rama I, starting this royal dynasty, which still exists today under Rama IX.
swap.clue: This is the name given to Thailand's ruling house. It was the original name of Rama I.
